_doc: Anti-drift compass for the PM SCHEDULER DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-28: 'let's now plan for another page' -> PM Scheduler, chosen after measuring the candidates). Companion to PM_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/pm_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per PMK class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new PMK dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the screens, handlers, tables and derived values the journey touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B at spoke 5; retrieve-first, crawl on a genuine bag miss
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

PM01.notes: First run - a hive with registered assets but no PM program yet. The empty/first-run state was never mapped by the PDDA arc. WALKED 2026-07-28 and found a DEAD EMPTY STATE - the D3 discrimination class on a client-filtered view. renderDashboard's zero-result branch showed #dash-empty for BOTH situations, and #dash-empty is the first-run onboarding CTA: 'No assets yet - Tap the + button to add your first asset and set up its PM schedule.' So a supervisor in Lucena - 31 REGISTERED PM assets - who tapped the 'On Track' chip (Lucena has 0 on track) was told their PM program was empty and instructed to create their first asset. The correctly-worded element existed the whole time: '#no-results - No PM tasks match those filters.' was authored, styled, and referenced NOWHERE in the code. A grep for 'no-results' returned exactly ONE hit, the markup line. Proven live before fixing: clicking On Track took the list 10 cards -> 0 cards with #no-results still hidden. AN INSTRUMENT CORRECTION EN ROUTE: my first attempt drove a bogus value into the category combobox and nothing happened - because that filter only applies on an EXACT match, so a typed-but-unknown value is correctly ignored. The page was right and my probe was wrong; the real path to a zero-result state is a status chip. FIXED by discriminating on enriched.length (did this hive EVER have assets?) rather than on the filtered count. Verified live in three states: normal 10 cards with neither message, filtered-to-nothing showing only 'No PM tasks match those filters.', and restored back to 10. GATED by extending tools/validate_empty_state_discrimination.py - the existing D3 gate from the logbook team-search bug - rather than writing a new one. It went RED on my correct fix first: its detector only recognised the `classList.remove('hidden')` idiom, while pm-scheduler's #no-results uses the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE. Taught the gate that shape (both are valid, and it was blind to the attribute idiom on ANY page) instead of bending the code. Teeth re-proven after teaching: reverting the fix -> exit 1.

PM02.notes: Register a PM asset -> scope items -> frequency. G: the PDDA arc mapped the 3-screen wizard (screen-dashboard / screen-add / screen-detail), saveAsset/saveNewTask, and the canonical FREQ registry + canonFreq(). WALKED 2026-07-28 - CLEAN on every axis this arc has reason to doubt. The asset insert CONFIRMS (.from('pm_assets').insert(payload).select().single()) and the scope-item insert confirms too, so neither can report a write that landed nowhere. Partial failure is reported HONESTLY: if the asset saves but its scope items fail, the toast says 'Asset saved but scope items failed. Please edit and retry.' rather than claiming the whole registration succeeded - the same discipline as the PM4 logbook mirror. AND IT CLOSES PM8's OPEN QUESTION: the frequency <select> is built from FREQ.map(f => f.key), so the six canonical keys are the ONLY values a user can choose. Combined with PM16's template audit, that makes the view's ELSE-30 catch-all UNREACHABLE from the UI - the latent bomb can only be armed by an import, and that path now routes through whFreqFromDays. SECOND PERSONA (worker) WALKED, and it completes the CRUD sweep on pm_assets that PM12 and PM3 started. goAddAsset() is supervisor-gated in the UI, but a WORKER inserting a pm_asset into their OWN hive succeeds at the database - 1 row, probed rolled-back. That is the THIRD verb of the same UI-only-gate class (PM12 closed DELETE, PM3 closed UPDATE, INSERT is still open). LOWER SEVERITY than the other two, stated plainly: the row lands in the worker's OWN hive and is self-authored, so it is not a cross-tenant hole. What it does allow is a member the UI says cannot add assets adding one anyway, which moves the PM compliance DENOMINATOR for their hive. NOT SHIPPED, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED rather than assumed: asset-hub's resolvePmAssetId() lazily CREATES a pm_assets row on demand when an RCM strategy is linked to a scope item, with no role gate of its own. A supervisor-only INSERT guard would break that flow for every worker using RCM - the same trap that would have broken all 90 asset renames in PM3, caught the same way. The fix pattern is already established (route the system-owned creation through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC, as sync_pm_asset_identity does, THEN add the guard) but it needs asset-hub's newRow construction moved into the function, so it is queued rather than rushed. The 72-of-91 worker-authored assets in the data are SEEDER output (service_role), not evidence that workers create assets through the page - checked, because that number would otherwise have argued the gate was wrong.

PM03.notes: The triage dashboard. G: the PDDA arc fixed worst-first sort (overdue was buried on page 2, now position 0) and getAssetOverallStatus. Per-ROLE triage is unwalked - a tech and a supervisor want different orderings. WALKED 2026-07-28. TWO ANSWERS. (1) THE TRIAGE VIEW IS THE SAME FOR BOTH ROLES, and that is HONEST rather than a gap: pm_scope_items has no assignee column (id, asset_id, hive_id, item_text, frequency, anchor_date, is_custom, created_at), so there is no data on which to personalise a tech's list. Worst-first for everyone is the correct design for this schema; personalising it would need a schema change, not a UI change. Role differentiation is therefore about WRITE affordances, and HIVE_ROLE is re-derived from live membership on load rather than trusted from cache - the role-gate-on-session rule already applied. (2) THE WRITE AFFORDANCE WAS UI-ONLY, the same class as PM12's delete. The page says 'Supervisors only.' when a worker taps Edit Asset, while pm_assets_write's USING was satisfied by ANY active member. Probed live: a WORKER renamed a supervisor's asset to 'HIJACKED' and set its criticality to Low - one row, no error. That is consequential: criticality feeds risk scoring, triage order and alert severity, and asset_name is how every surface identifies the machine. THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE PLATFORM, and measuring first is the only reason it did not ship. Mirroring the delete guard ('supervisor OR the asset's author') would also have refused logbook.html's syncToPMAssets, which propagates a rename from asset_nodes into pm_assets. Measured: of 90 pm_asset<->node pairs, ALL 90 have a node author different from the pm_asset author, and in all 90 that author is not a supervisor. Every rename on the platform would have matched 0 rows - and a 0-row UPDATE is not an error, so the existing `if (error)` warning would never have fired. The name would have silently diverged between asset_nodes and pm_assets: a cross-surface identity split, the exact class this platform has spent arcs closing. FIXED IN THE RIGHT ORDER, three verified slices. 20260728000008 makes the propagation a SECURITY DEFINER RPC (sync_pm_asset_identity) that checks hive membership itself and can only touch asset_name/tag_id, so it is not a back door around the supervisor gate; logbook.html now calls it and warns when a rename matches nothing; then 20260728000009 adds the restrictive UPDATE guard. Proven together: worker direct edit -> 0 rows, worker rename via the RPC -> 1 row, supervisor direct edit -> 1 row, and a cross-hive rename through the RPC -> 0 rows with the foreign name unchanged. GATED: validate_pm_write_isolation 10 -> 12 checks, asserting BOTH halves, because they are only safe as a pair - the guard without the RPC is the silent-divergence bug. Teeth proven by dropping the guard (exit 1).

PM04.notes: Complete a PM at the asset (checklist, readings, sign-off). G: pmCompleteHandler + markDone mapped; the completion writes pm_completions and mirrors to logbook. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE WRITE PATH IS SOUND, and checked against the two failure shapes this arc found elsewhere. (1) It CONFIRMS: .insert(compPayload).select().single(), so a write that lands nowhere cannot be reported as saved - the LG3 shape does not apply here. (2) It already treats 23505 as EXACTLY-ONCE: a double-tap hits pm_completions_dedup_uidx and the page says 'Already recorded for this task today' rather than a scary failure. That is the SAME reasoning I applied to the offline drain in PM18, arrived at independently by the page months earlier - so the online and offline paths now agree instead of one calling a saved PM stuck. (3) NO HIDDEN-FIELD LEAK: the logbook arc's LB03 defect was a hidden section whose inputs were still collected. The PM completion sheet has exactly THREE inputs (findings, action, log toggle) and zero conditional or hidden blocks, so the class cannot occur - a real clean result, checked rather than assumed. (4) The logbook mirror's failure is reported HONESTLY: if the PM saves but the mirror fails, the toast says 'PM saved -> PM compliance updated. Logbook entry failed: check connection' instead of claiming both. The at-the-asset tap target for this journey was 36px and is now 44px (PM15).

PM05.notes: PRIORITY. Complete -> next_due_date recompute -> the card changes state. G partial: the PDDA arc verified ONE reschedule loop live (overdue Weekly -> complete -> next_due +7), but the recompute is DERIVED in v_pm_scope_items_truth and its completeness across frequency bands and personas is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ARITHMETIC IS CLEAN: next_due_date is DERIVED in v_pm_scope_items_truth from COALESCE(last_completed_at, anchor_date, created_at) + frequency_days, and every consumer reads the derived columns rather than recomputing - alert-hub, dayplanner, hive and logbook all select is_overdue / days_until_due / next_due_date straight from the view, and hive.html documents deleting its own HIVE_FREQ_DAYS map on 2026-05-20 for exactly this reason. So a completion re-derives everywhere by construction, and PMK4 now pins the frequency_days half of that derivation against the client. Recorded as a real clean result. THE DEFECT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE TRANSITION - WHETHER THE READER IS TOLD WHAT THEY ARE LOOKING AT. analytics.html renders analytics_snapshots: the first view of the PHT day computes and saves, every later view replays the saved copy, and only Refresh recomputes. Good feature. But the source chip hardcoded 'Live recomputation each refresh' on EVERY load. Measured: the KPI numbers were on screen at 0ms, up to ~24h old, under a chip promising they were live. In this journey's terms: a tech completes a PM, opens analytics, compliance has not moved, and nothing says the number predates their work. FIXED: the chip now reports which of the two it actually is, per phase (one tab can be a snapshot while another was just recomputed) - 'Saved snapshot, computed 1 min ago - Refresh to recompute' vs 'Recomputed just now', verified live in both states and both languages. Three call sites had to be reconciled, because the chip is first drawn BEFORE hydration decides snapshot-vs-live: the live fetch, the post-hydration render, and the phase switch. My first attempt fixed only the live path and the cached load kept the false claim - the same two-render-paths mistake PMK1 caught, made twice in one arc. GATED by tools/validate_source_chip_freshness.py (registered): a page reading a *_snapshots/*_cache table must COMPUTE its freshness string, never hardcode a liveness claim. The existing 'Source-chip truth' dimension only checks that a chip names views the page READS, which is how this shipped green. Teeth proven by restoring the hardcoded claim: exit 1.

PM06.notes: Completion -> logbook mirror (pm_completion_id lineage). G: gate #27 pm_mirror_asset_lineage locks the CREATE lineage, and the logbook arc seeded 40 mirrored completions so the journey is finally demonstrable (it was 0/1591 before). WALKED 2026-07-28 and the lineage is SOUND - recorded as a real clean result. 40 logbook rows mirror a PM completion: 0 dangling, 0 sitting in a different hive from their completion, and 40 of 40 carry node lineage (asset_node_id). The logbook arc's seeder is what made this demonstrable at all; before it, 0 of 1,591 completions carried a pm_completion_id. THE FK's SET NULL IS THE RIGHT DISPOSITION, checked rather than assumed: deleting a completion (including via the PM12 asset cascade) leaves the logbook entry standing with its pointer nulled. The entry is the technician's own written record and must survive; and its MEANING survives the lost pointer too, because the row still reads maintenance_type='Preventive Maintenance' / 'Scheduled PM'. CASCADE would delete a worker's record to tidy a foreign key; RESTRICT would block a legitimate asset deletion. GAP RECORDED, NOT INVENTED AWAY: logbook.html contains ZERO references to pm_completion_id, so the page never links a mirrored entry back to the PM that produced it. The reader can tell it IS a PM from the text; what is missing is the click-through. That is a UX addition rather than a defect fix, so it is written here instead of built mid-arc - the same call made for PM9's missing skip UI. GATE ADDED because the existing one could not see this: validate_pm asserts the PAGE SENDS pm_completion_id, and that check passed for months while no row actually had one. A payload check cannot see dangling or cross-hive mirrors, so validate_pm_write_isolation grew a 10th check on the DATA (a mirror in a different hive from its completion is a tenancy leak through the back door: an entry in hive A citing hive B's work). MY OWN MISTAKE, recorded: the teeth test mutated a REAL logbook row's hive_id and my note called it 'rolled back' when it was not in a transaction. Caught immediately, restored by rejoining the row to its completion's hive (1 row, 0 cross-hive remaining, gate back to 10/10). A walk can consume its own fixture - restore it, and do not label a bare UPDATE as rolled back.

PM07.notes: THE KEYSTONE. MEASURED 2026-07-28 before this roadmap existed: across 1,224 consecutive-completion intervals, 331 (27.0%) were completed AFTER frequency_days had elapsed, and 14.5% at more than 1.5x the interval - while get_pm_compliance_smrp reports 85.7-87.5% per hive, which reads as near-world-class against the 90% benchmark. The RPC counts a completion whenever it lands in the period, regardless of whether it was on schedule. HARVESTED (bag miss -> crawl): the SMRP-derived standard states PM compliance = completed / scheduled x 100, world-class 90%, and explicitly that it 'does not account for late PMs' (substrate/external/external-pm-schedule-compliance-metric.md). W/R open: the walk needs 2 personas x 2 states, and the disposition (surface on-time% beside compliance% vs change the metric) is a judgement to make WITH the walk, not before it. WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28, TWO personas in TWO hives, and the contradiction is on the glass: supervisor/Lucena sees '0 of 31 on track now - 88% PM compliance (SMRP)' with 20 overdue, and worker/Manila sees '3 of 30 on track now - 86% PM compliance (SMRP)' with 24 overdue. The page's headline ('PM compliance is in the red') and its next-action ('Assign 24 overdue PMs') are honest; the SMRP figure sits in the ON TRACK card's subtitle right beside the real-time count, so a historical late-blind metric reads as reassurance about the present. QUANTIFIED by the new detector: compliance 86.3% vs on-time 73.0% = a 13.3-POINT flattery. R PARTIAL and deliberately so: the gap is now MEASURED and ratcheted (tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py, registered, teeth proven), but SURFACING an on-time figure beside the compliance figure is a product change to a number a plant acts on - that is the next unit, not a drive-by. CLOSED 2026-07-28. The measure existed only inside a validator's SQL, so the page still showed only the flattering half. Built get_pm_ontime_delivery (migration 20260728000005) as the ONE definition - hive-scoped, period-aware, membership-gated the same way as get_pm_compliance_smrp (both a foreign hive and a NULL platform-wide read from an authenticated caller are rejected 42501, probed). get_pm_compliance_smrp is deliberately UNCHANGED: it implements a named standard and holds verified parity with analytics. SURFACED on the PM Scheduler card as '72.5% done on time - 123 of 447 ran late' beside the 88%, with the late COUNT named because that is the form a supervisor can act on. Walked in both hives: Lucena 88/72.5, Manila 86/74.7, each matching the DB exactly. THE FULL-PAGE VIEW FOUND WHAT THE CARD DID NOT: the page said 'PM compliance is in the red - 29 assets are overdue' in its banner and 'STAIR-READY' on this card at 0 of 31 on track, because the tag read compliance alone and 88 >= 80. The ladder now runs on the WEAKER of compliance and on-time - same 80/60 thresholds, no invented standard, on the principle that a program is only as ready as its weakest measure. Safe because the canonical maturity Stair is a composite from compute_hive_readiness (canonical/standards.json), which this local heuristic only ever approximated; the analytics arc had already grepped that overall_pct is not consumed by hive_readiness. Lucena now reads BUILDING/amber and no longer contradicts its own banner. CLS: the new line reserves the two lines it fills (measured 31px at 390px and desktop), so it costs zero shift.

PM08.notes: Change an asset's frequency -> the whole schedule re-derives. G partial: the frequency VOCABULARY is canonical and gated (canonFreq + freq_crosspage_consistent), and asset-hub's RCM interval writer was fixed - but a frequency CHANGE on an existing program, and whether every derived surface re-derives, is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28 and the defect is upstream of the change itself. A PM's frequency is a WORD in the DB, and the schedule is DERIVED from that word by a CASE in v_pm_scope_items_truth - so every writer that turns an interval in DAYS into that word is deciding the real schedule, and TWO of them did it differently. integrations.html (the CMMS/CSV import a plant uses to onboard its EXISTING program) had a local map with NO Daily bucket, taking the first bucket >= days over [7,30,90,180,365]: measured, 1 day -> 'Weekly' (7x rarer than the source system asked), 14 -> 'Monthly' (2.1x), 45 -> 'Quarterly' (2x). Every drift ran the SAME direction, less often than specified - the direction that leaves equipment un-inspected. asset-hub.html rounded to the NEAREST bucket instead, so a 300-day RCM interval became 'Annual' (365). FIXED with ONE shared mapping (whFreqFromDays / whFreqDays in utils.js, loaded platform-wide) that snaps DOWN to the closest bucket not exceeding the requested interval: rounding to a shorter interval costs labour, rounding to a longer one is a safety decision. Verified live on integrations.html: 1/2/3d now Daily, 14d Weekly, 45d Monthly, 300d Semi-Annual, and zero intervals in 1..400 remain rarer than asked. The only floor is sub-daily (0.5d -> Daily), which the six-label vocabulary genuinely cannot express. ALSO PINNED, LATENT: the UI's canonFreq resolves 'biweekly'/'fortnightly' to Weekly (7d) while the view says 14d - so such a row would show a Weekly badge on a fortnightly schedule. No such rows exist (all 416 scope items map cleanly: weekly 102, monthly 99, quarterly 93, annual 91, semi-annual 31), making this the logbook arc's LG2 shape - agreement by luck of vocabulary - so the gate asserts it rather than waiting for the first import that uses the word. The view's ELSE 30 catch-all is the same bomb: 'Every 500 hours' displays as the UI's 'Other' bucket while the DB silently schedules it monthly. GATED by tools/validate_pm_frequency_mapping.py (parity live vs utils.js, safe-direction over 1..400, and no page carrying a private bucket list), registered in run_platform_checks; teeth proven by restoring the private map (exit 1) and reverting (exit 0).

PM09.notes: Skip / defer a PM. pm_completions carries status='skipped' (~5% of seeded rows) but nothing models what a skip MEANS in the compliance number - neither silently compliant nor silently overdue. Feeds PMK5. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ANSWER TO THE JOURNEY'S QUESTION IS YES - the numbers are honest, and that is a real result, not an absence of one. Proven in a rolled-back transaction: inserting a status='skipped' completion moved neither the hive's compliance (85.7 -> 85.7) nor the scope item's next_due_date. A skip therefore cannot be used to clear an overdue flag or flatter the program. That honesty rests on three independent status='done' filters (the compliance RPC, the on-time RPC, and the truth view's last_completed_at LATERAL), any one of which a later edit could drop, so it is now asserted rather than left to luck - teeth proven by replacing the on-time RPC with one that omits the filter (exit 1). AN INSTRUMENT ERROR OF MY OWN, caught before it became a false finding: grepping the pages for the literal 'skipped' returned nothing outside backup dirs, and I nearly recorded 'no surface shows a skip'. The detail view DOES render them - it tests c.status === 'done' ? 'Completed' : 'Deferred', so it matches on the COMPLEMENT and my literal grep could never have found it. THE REAL GAP IS REACHABILITY, recorded honestly rather than papered over: 78 skipped rows exist and render as 'Deferred' in the per-asset history, but NOTHING in the page can create one. A technician who cannot do a PM has no way to say so - the choice is to leave it overdue (indistinguishable from untouched) or mark it done, which is a lie. Building that flow is a product decision, not a defect fix, so it is written here rather than invented mid-arc. The related triage gap: the dashboard cannot distinguish overdue-and-untouched from deferred-with-a-reason. FIXTURE FIXED (the seeder decides what can be tested - HK2's lesson again): status and note were drawn INDEPENDENTLY, so 'skipped' rows carried completion notes - 78 skips saying things like 'All readings nominal', which is incoherent, since if the readings were nominal the PM was done. Status and note are now generated together (_completion_status_and_note) with real skip reasons - 'Line still running, could not isolate', 'Deferred: no spare gasket in stores'. Verified over 400 draws: 29 skips, 0 incoherent.

PM10.notes: Compliance rollup parity across page / analytics / hive PM Health / shift-brain. G: the PDDA arc verified SMRP 87.1% single-RPC parity between page and analytics. The other two consumers, and parity under a CHANGED program, are unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28 across all three surfaces. THE NUMBERS AGREE: pm-scheduler shows 87.5 (rendered 88) and 72.5% on time for Lucena, analytics shows the same 88 / 72.5 from the same RPCs, and every figure matches the DB exactly. Parity held even though this arc had just CHANGED the analytics card, which is what made the check worth running when it was. AND A RECALL THAT PREVENTED A FALSE BUG: hive said '29 PMs overdue' while the DB has 40 overdue scope items in Lucena, which looks like an under-count - but the derivation carries an explicit 2026-06-09 comment saying the roll-up counts ASSETS on purpose, so the tile matches the PM Scheduler it deep-links to (counting items there once showed '9 overdue' against the scheduler's '6'). The COUNT was never wrong. Recalling the disposition before declaring the bug is exactly the discipline that saved this one. THE REAL DEFECT IS THE NOUN, and it is PMK1's class on a different surface: the same asset-scoped number was labelled four different ways in ONE page - the tile 'PM tasks overdue', the nudge '29 PMs overdue', the CTA 'Assign 29 overdue PMs', a notification 'PM Tasks Overdue' - while only the banner said '29 assets with overdue PM'. In Lucena that is 29 assets against 40 actual overdue tasks, so a supervisor reading '29 PMs' plans for 29 jobs and meets 40, a 38% under-statement of the work. SIX sites fixed in EN and FIL (the first sweep caught three; a second grep found three more - fix every path, not just the walked one), verified live in both languages, with the rationale recorded at the derivation so the next reader does not 'fix' the deliberate asset-scoping. GATED by a noun-scope check in validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance (same class, same gate); teeth proven by restoring one old string: exit 1.

PM11.notes: PRIORITY. Amend or delete a completion after sign-off. O partial on MEASURED evidence from the logbook arc's LG4 sweep: pm_completions has 6 user triggers and NONE of them audit, so an amendment by any path that skips the page leaves no record - exactly the weakness LG4 closed for logbook with trg_logbook_post_close_audit. HARVEST: that arc's own finding plus the pattern and migration to copy (20260728000003). Feeds PMK3. WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28 and the defect is the sharp version. A technician silently BACK-DATED their own completion by 400 days: one row affected, no error, nothing recorded anywhere. completed_at is the most consequential field on a compliance record - it drives the compliance window, the on-time measure and next_due_date - so moving it moves the number a plant and an auditor both read: back-dating a late PM makes it on-time. Unlike logbook, there was no client-written audit row either, so the trigger is not a backstop here, it is the ONLY record there has ever been. FIXED by migration 20260728000004: an AFTER UPDATE trigger recording amend_pm_completion with completed_at before/after, status before/after, and days_moved - the number an auditor actually wants. Scoped to fields that change what the record CLAIMS (completed_at / status / scope_item_id), so a notes edit stays silent and the log remains readable enough to be audited. Proven in a rolled-back transaction: insert 0 rows, notes-edit 0 rows, back-date 1 row with days_moved -400.00. The probe row was restored exactly. GATED by extending tools/validate_pm_write_isolation.py (the arc's own gate template) from 4 checks to 5; teeth proven by dropping the trigger (exit 1) and re-applying (exit 0).

PM12.notes: Delete a PM asset -> what happens to its scope items, its completion history and the compliance denominator. The 2 unconfirmed DB writes (pm_assets update + delete, ~L2640) live here. Feeds PMK6. WALKED 2026-07-28 and it is the most consequential defect of the arc so far. pm_completions.asset_id and pm_scope_items.asset_id both CASCADE from pm_assets, so deleting one asset destroys its whole compliance history. Probed live in a rolled-back transaction as a WORKER: deleting 'Caterpillar 3516B' took 31 completion records and 8 scope items, history reaching back to 2026-04-29, and left ZERO audit rows at the database. Those 31 rows are the evidence that named people did named jobs on dated occasions; they feed compliance %, on-time delivery and the reliability figures downstream, so the deletion also rewrites HISTORICAL compliance. TWO SEPARATE HOLES. (1) AUTHORIZATION: pm-scheduler gates the Delete button to a supervisor or the asset's author and even toasts 'Only supervisors can delete other members' assets' - but that rule lived ONLY in the page. pm_assets_write is a single ALL policy satisfied by ANY active member, so a worker writing through the db client deleted a supervisor's asset. The canonical UI-only-gate-is-bypassable class, with the sharpest possible payload. (2) EVIDENCE: there was no DELETE trigger on pm_assets at all; the only record was one the PAGE wrote afterwards, which any non-page write skips - and which never knew what the cascade cost. FIXED by migration 20260728000006: a RESTRICTIVE DELETE policy (ANDed with the existing permissive one, the smallest change that cannot widen anything else) matching the rule the UI already states, plus a BEFORE DELETE trigger that counts the children while they still exist and records completions_destroyed / scope_items_destroyed / history_began. Proven: WORKER delete -> 0 rows, SUPERVISOR delete -> 1 row, audit meta reads {completions_destroyed: 31, scope_items_destroyed: 8, history_began: 2026-04-29}. THE CLIENT ALSO CLAIMED A REFUSED DELETE AS DONE: deleteAsset() tested only `if (error)`, and a PostgREST delete matching nothing returns error:null - so it toasted success, wrote an audit row for a deletion that never happened, and dropped the asset locally so it silently returned on reload. The restrictive policy makes that path REACHABLE rather than theoretical, so it is now confirmed with .select('id'); the client-side audit write was deleted outright because the trigger supersedes it and duplicating it would double-count. GATED: validate_pm_write_isolation grew from 5 checks to 8 (delete_role_gated live-probes a worker deleting an asset they did not author; delete_audited and delete_policy_present assert the trigger and policy survive a later migration). Teeth proven by dropping the policy: 2 checks fail, exit 1.

PM13.notes: Cross-hive boundary: a foreign completion must not inflate another hive's compliance. G: ALREADY HARDENED by the PDDA arc - 3 write holes fixed by migration 20260712000012, gate validate_pm_write_isolation.py 4/4, and get_pm_compliance_smrp raises 42501 for a non-member. The walk re-confirms it from the UI side across personas rather than re-litigating it. WALKED 2026-07-28 and found a REAL cross-tenant hole the PDDA arc's own xcomp test could not catch. pm_completions_write's WITH CHECK required that the row's ASSET belong to the same hive as its hive_id (mig 20260712000012), and said NOTHING about scope_item_id. So a member of hive A could insert a completion with hive_id = their OWN hive (passes membership), asset_id = their OWN asset (passes the existing parent check), and scope_item_id = a scope item in hive B - and it was ACCEPTED. WHY THAT MATTERS: every consumer joins completions to scope items by scope_item_id, NOT by the completion's own hive_id. get_pm_compliance_smrp counts per scope item, so the foreign hive's credited completions went 502 -> 503 from one row. get_pm_ontime_delivery counts the same intervals. And v_pm_scope_items_truth's last_completed_at takes the newest completion for the item, which drives next_due_date - so the row silently CLEARS an overdue PM in another plant. That last consequence is the sharp one: it does not just move a percentage, it removes work from someone else's overdue list. xcomp misses it because that probe sets hive_id to the FOREIGN hive (correctly blocked). Aiming hive_id at your OWN hive while pointing scope_item_id at theirs slips through the gap BETWEEN the two columns - a child/ledger-table WITH CHECK that validates one parent and not the other. FIXED by migration 20260728000007: a RESTRICTIVE policy requiring the scope item to belong to the SAME ASSET the completion names. Since the existing check already ties that asset to the hive, one condition closes both the tenancy hole and the nonsense pairing. Verified safe BEFORE applying: of 1,591 completions, zero have a scope item in another hive, on another asset, or a NULL scope_item_id, so it rejects nothing that exists. NULL scope_item_id still passes, for a future ad-hoc completion. GATED as a 9th check in validate_pm_write_isolation; teeth proven by dropping the policy (the probe reports OPEN_VULN, exit 1) and re-applying (exit 0). A GATE-HARNESS BUG OF MY OWN, found because the whole probe went silent: my new SQL comment contained an EM DASH, and psql input piped through subprocess on Windows is encoded cp1252, so Postgres rejected the batch with 'invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0x97' and NONE of the five RESULT lines were emitted. Every check read None and the gate reported 5 failures that were really one encoding error. SQL sent through subprocess must be pure ASCII.

PM14.notes: Parts / readings on a PM. G: the PDDA arc's reuse verdict was completion->logbook = the canonical FUSION (one event) and parts-on-a-PM = KEEP-DISTINCT (logbook owns parts). The walk tests whether that boundary holds for a tech who consumed parts during a PM. WALKED 2026-07-28 as the reuse boundary it is, and the boundary is DELIBERATE and coherent. The PM completion captures a light sign-off only - findings and action - and does NOT capture parts or readings. Those live in the logbook, and the completion's log toggle mirrors into a real logbook row the same worker owns (auth_uid set, asset_node_id resolved, pm_completion_id linked), which they can then open and enrich with the parts picker. So the capability is not missing, it is two steps: sign off the PM, then add parts to the entry it created. KEEP-DISTINCT is the right verdict - duplicating a parts picker into the PM sheet would put a second writer on inventory_transactions, which is precisely the ledger-tamper class the platform has spent two arcs closing. RECORDED AS A FRICTION, not a defect: a tech whose PM consumed a filter has to remember the second step, and nothing on the PM sheet tells them the mirrored entry is where parts go. A one-line hint on the sheet would close it without duplicating the writer. Written here rather than built mid-arc, same call as PM9's skip UI and PM6's missing back-link. THE MIRROR PAYLOAD ITSELF IS WELL-FORMED, and its comments record three earlier bugs worth not repeating: logbook.id is TEXT NOT NULL with no default (omitting it 23502'd every mirror), machine must be the asset TAG not the display name (every machine-keyed consumer and v_logbook_truth expect the tag), and auth_uid + asset_node_id were both being dropped, orphaning the row from attribution and from v_asset_truth history.

PM15.notes: Mobile 390px at-the-asset completion - the tech is THE persona for this page. G partial: the PDDA arc's A-axis was axe-clean (0 violations) but axe measures a11y, not one-handed reachability of the completion flow. WALKED 2026-07-28 at a TRUE 390px viewport with ufai_battery.js v1.6.2 (the existing instrument - not hand-rolled probes). AN INSTRUMENT ERROR FIRST, because it invalidates how earlier numbers in this arc were obtained: browser_resize(390) produced window.innerWidth = 585. The browser runs at devicePixelRatio 0.667 (~67% zoom), so every width I set came back 1.5x wider - the 'desktop 1280' reads were really 1920. Detected only because the battery echoed innerWidth. Corrected by setting 260x563 to land a true 390x845, and the PM7 CLS reserve was RE-MEASURED there: still 2 lines, deficit 0, no spill, no horizontal scroll - the conclusion held, but it had been reached at the wrong width. Verify the instrument BEFORE the page, again. THE WORKED STATE IS WHERE THE DEFECTS LIVE: the dashboard scored 0 usability defects; the ASSET DETAIL - the screen this journey is actually about - scored 10. Measuring the landing state would have reported a clean page. FIXED, all page-owned: .complete-btn 36x36 -> 44x44 (the PRIMARY at-the-asset action, a technician at a machine and often gloved, recording that a PM was done - it was the smallest target on the screen after the shared chrome, and WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor is not the right bar for the one control the whole journey exists to press); #btn-edit-asset and #btn-delete-asset 40px tall -> 44; both goBack() buttons 54x20 -> 44 high (Major severity, the shortest target on the page); loadMoreHistory 320x38 -> 44. CLS 0.13 -> 0.092, under the 0.1 budget, by reserving the two summary sub-lines that grow when data lands: pm-ontrack-sub fills to THREE lines at 390px (deficit 31px) and pm-duesoon-sub to two (15px). This is the pre-existing row-growth carried out of the PM7 walk, now measured and closed rather than left as a note. RESULT: 10 defects -> 0 on the detail screen and 0 on the dashboard, both at a true 390px. The shared companion/feedback chrome (17-22px controls) also cleared. Not this page's to fix and not claimed as such: they belong to the shared widget and are recorded for the chrome owner.

PM16.notes: Templates + scope-item reuse across assets. G partial: populateTemplateOptions / selectTmplCat / pickTaskChip mapped; whether a template edit propagates to assets already using it is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28 - CLEAN, and it supplies the last piece of PM8's reachability proof. Audited every frequency literal in PM_TEMPLATES: exactly four distinct values (Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Yearly), ALL in the canonical vocabulary - 'Yearly' resolves through canonFreq to Annual and the view maps it to 365. So no template can plant a scope item that silently becomes a 30-day schedule. Templates route through canonFreq on both the wizard path (freq: canonFreq(t.freq) || t.freq) and the save path, and custom items go through the same constrained <select>. Combined with PM2, every UI path into pm_scope_items.frequency is vocabulary-bounded, so the view's ELSE 30 is dead code from the UI's side - it can only be reached by an import, which PM8 fixed.

PM17.notes: Shift-brain 'PMs Due' + the AI companion grounding must read the same truth as the page. G partial: setPmCompanionContext ships a piiSafe snapshot (registered live by the PDDA arc); the shift-planner-orchestrator's PM read is a separate path and unverified against the page. WALKED 2026-07-28 across the AI surfaces, and found the SAME noun/scope defect PM10 fixed on the hive board - this time in the grounding, which is the worst place for it. agentic-rag-loop gets it RIGHT and says so: it selects pm_asset_id and takes new Set(...).size, with an explicit comment that canonical PM-overdue is DISTINCT pm_asset_id and 'Matches the tiles'. ai-gateway's buildProactiveBriefing got it WRONG: a head-count of v_pm_scope_items_truth rows filtered is_overdue - which counts SCOPE ITEMS - phrased as '${n} PM tasks overdue'. Measured in Lucena that is 40 against the 29 assets every screen reports, so the proactive briefing would open with '40 PM tasks overdue' to a supervisor whose board, PM Scheduler card and other AI lane all say 29. WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE: the companion is the surface a user is least able to check. On a page they can click through and count; in a briefing they can only believe it. Holding the minority definition there turns a labelling inconsistency into a trust problem, and it is the third place this arc has found a count and its noun disagreeing (analytics 'PMs on time', hive 'PM tasks overdue', now the briefing). FIXED to count distinct pm_asset_id and to SAY assets, matching agentic-rag-loop and the tiles. Verified the function still loads and serves in the local edge runtime (400 'Missing agent' on an empty body = alive, not a syntax error). shift-brain reads from the shift-planner-orchestrator, which draws v_risk_truth + v_pm_scope_items_truth - the same canonical source, so no third definition exists.

PM18.notes: Offline completion at the asset - the plant has no signal where the machine is. pm-scheduler registers a shared queue (window._whPmQueue via whCreateQueue, table pm_completions), which the logbook arc's LG3 fix now protects from reporting a lost write as synced. The journey itself is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE GOOD RESULT FIRST: pm-scheduler queues its completion through the SHARED whCreateQueue, so it inherited the logbook arc's 0-row confirmation fix without any change here - which is exactly what a shared component is for, and worth recording as a real result rather than an absence of one. THE DEFECT IS THE OPPOSITE ERROR. pm-scheduler's own comment claimed 'the dedup UNIQUE index makes a reconnect re-insert benign'. Half true: the index prevents a duplicate ROW, but the drain does a plain .insert() and does not know that. If the write LANDS and the reply is lost - the ordinary brownout case this queue exists for - the item stays queued, the next drain re-inserts, and pm_completions_dedup_uidx (scope_item_id, worker_name, completed_at::date) raises 23505. The drain recorded that as an error, rode the backoff to MAX_RETRIES, and dead-lettered the item, so the connectivity widget told the worker their PM was STUCK when it was already saved. That is the exact MIRROR of the LG3 bug the same drain was fixed for: one claimed a write that never happened, this denies one that did. Both leave the worker unable to trust what the app says about their own work. Proven at the DB: the first insert succeeds, the retry raises 23505. FIXED in the shared drain: a 23505 on insert now drains the item as already-applied, which is precisely what a dedup index is FOR. Deliberately OPT-IN (insertDedupIndexed) rather than default, because it is only sound where the unique index is a true idempotency key for the same logical write - pm_completions' is (only this worker's own retry of the same PM on the same day can collide), but skill_profiles.worker_name is NOT, since there a 23505 means a DIFFERENT row owns the key and the write genuinely did not land. Measured across the queue's tables: only pm_completions, inventory_items, rcm_fmea_modes and skill_profiles carry a business unique index at all, so defaulting it on would have changed semantics for surfaces nobody has walked. GATED: validate_offline_queue_confirm grew a retry-idempotency check asserting BOTH halves - the shared drain still recognises 23505 under the flag, the flag still defaults to false, and pm-scheduler still opts in. Teeth proven three ways (remove the opt-in -> exit 1; default the flag to true -> exit 1; restore -> exit 0).

PMK1.name: On-time is not the same as done
PMK1.notes: OPEN on measured evidence. RULE: a compliance metric must distinguish a PM completed ON SCHEDULE from one completed late, or it flatters the program to the person least able to check it. EVIDENCE (2026-07-28): 331 of 1,224 intervals (27.0%) ran past frequency_days, 14.5% past 1.5x, while the RPC reports 85.7-87.5%. HARVEST: crawled on a genuine bag miss - the corpus held 144 external chunks and NOT ONE on maintenance; substrate/external/external-pm-schedule-compliance-metric.md now states the formula, the 90% world-class benchmark, and the explicit blind spot ('does not account for late PMs'). DETECT/FIX/GATE open: the disposition is a real judgement (surface an on-time% beside compliance%, vs change what compliance means) and belongs WITH the walk, since changing a number a plant acts on is not a drive-by. DETECT DONE: tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py computes both figures like-for-like (it mirrors the RPC's own scheduled-count so the comparison is fair) and holds the GAP as a forward-only ratchet at 13.3 points. SWEEP DONE: the metric has exactly one producer - get_pm_compliance_smrp - which every consumer (page, analytics, hive PM Health, shift-brain) reads, so there is no second definition to reconcile; the class is about what that one definition CANNOT SEE, not about drift between definitions. FIX/GATE remain open: the gate exists but the product still shows only the flattering number, and deciding whether to surface on-time% beside it, or to change what compliance means, is a judgement for Ian since it moves a figure a plant acts on and is covered by a named standard. SWEEP DONE - and the sibling held the SHARPER version of the defect. analytics.html labelled the SMRP completed/scheduled counts '541 of 618 PMs on time'. Those counts say nothing about lateness; the standard explicitly does not account for late PMs, and 27.0% of 1,224 intervals ran past their own frequency. The words 'on time' claimed the one thing the number cannot support, in both EN and FIL ('nasa oras'). Relabelled to 'PMs completed' / 'natapos', and the real figure added from the same RPC. Two stale code comments quoting the old label (descriptive.py, validate_pm_compliance_weighted.py) were corrected in the same change. TWO MORE FOUND IN THE SAME CARD: (1) its ladder used 'LOW', the ambiguous string that was fixed to 'BELOW STAIR' on the PM card in the 2026-05-14 walkthrough and never swept here; (2) the label and footnote both read '30 days' STATICALLY while the page defaults to 90 and never rewrote them on a period switch - so a 90-day number was labelled 30 days in both languages. Both now written from the payload's own period_days, verified across a FIL round-trip and a live 30<->90 switch. A TIMING BUG OF MY OWN, caught by verifying rather than assuming: the summary renders from TWO paths and the cached one (loadSnapshots) paints without ever calling fetchPhase, so the first version of this fix silently never showed the figure on the common load. Fixed by firing on both paths and repainting when the RPC lands.
PMK1.gate: tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py (gap ratchet + RPC/inline parity, per hive)

PMK2.name: A derived schedule needs a real denominator
PMK2.notes: OPEN on measured evidence, and deliberately framed as LATENT-AND-CONTAINED rather than 'compliance is wrong'. get_pm_compliance_smrp charges GREATEST(1, period/frequency_days) scheduled events, so in a 90-day window a Semi-annual PM (31 items) counts as 1 when it is truly due 0.5 times and an Annual PM (91 items) counts as 1 against a true 0.25 - 122 of 416 scope items (29%) structurally over-counted. MEASURED IMPACT TODAY: under one point per hive (85.7->85.3, 85.7->86.1, 87.5->87.1), because those items happen to carry completions in the window. So the honest disposition is the LG2 one: allow the approximation, make divergence detectable, and let a gate catch the day the data stops being kind. Same source as PMK1.

PMK3.name: Completion immutability is tamper-EVIDENT at the database
PMK3.notes: EARNED BY THE PM11 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: for a record that drives a regulated number, 'tamper-evident' has to mean the DATABASE recorded the amendment - a client-written row is skipped by any write that does not go through the page, and here there was no client-written row at all. EVIDENCE: a completion back-dated 400 days, silently, by its own author (pm_completions RLS is owner-scoped write, so this is a legitimate author doing an illegitimate thing). HARVEST: the logbook arc's LG4, whose migration and scoping decision transferred directly. FIX + GATE as recorded on PM11. SWEEP PARTIAL: inventory_items carries the same client-only-audit weakness (measured in the logbook arc's LG4 sweep, still unfixed) and pm_assets/pm_scope_items have not been checked for whether their amendments matter the same way. SWEEP COMPLETED BY PM12: tamper-evidence has to cover DESTRUCTION, not just amendment. A completion cannot be silently edited any more, but until 20260728000006 the entire history could be removed by deleting its parent asset - a bigger hole reached by a different door, and open to any member rather than the record's author. The general rule: for a record that drives a regulated number, enumerate every path that can CHANGE OR REMOVE it (direct update, parent cascade, bulk delete) and make each one leave a database-level trace. The trigger must run BEFORE the cascade, or the thing worth recording - how much was destroyed - is already gone.

PMK4.name: The word that sets the schedule must mean the same thing to every writer
PMK4.notes: EARNED BY THE PM08 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: when a schedule is DERIVED from a stored label, the label-producing code IS the scheduler. Any page converting a duration into that label must use ONE shared mapping whose day-values equal the deriving view's, and must round toward MORE frequent - under-scheduling a PM is a safety decision, over-scheduling is a cost one. EVIDENCE: two writers, two rules, neither matching the view; the CMMS import silently made every sub-weekly PM weekly. DISTINCT FROM PMK1 (which is about a metric flattering what was DONE) - this is about the SCHEDULE ITSELF being quietly wrong before any work happens. SWEEP: both known writers fixed; the gate fails any third page that grows its own bucket list.

PMK5.name: A count and its NOUN must agree, on every surface that quotes it
PMK5.notes: EARNED BY THREE INDEPENDENT INSTANCES in one arc, which is what makes it a class rather than three incidents. RULE: whenever a number is quoted to a user, the NOUN must name what was actually counted, and every surface quoting the same underlying figure must count it the same way. A number is a claim; its unit is part of the claim. INSTANCE 1 (PM7, analytics): the SMRP completed/scheduled counts were labelled '541 of 618 PMs ON TIME'. The standard explicitly does not account for late PMs and 27% of intervals ran late - the words claimed the one thing the number could not support. INSTANCE 2 (PM10, hive board): a deliberately ASSET-scoped overdue count was labelled 'PM tasks' / 'PMs' in four places and 'assets' in one - 29 assets against 40 actual overdue tasks, a 38% under-statement on the tile whose whole job is saying how much work there is. INSTANCE 3 (PM17, ai-gateway): the proactive briefing head-counted scope-item rows and said '40 PM tasks overdue' where every screen said 29. Worst placement of the three: on a page a user can click through and count, in a briefing they can only believe it. WHAT THE THREE HAVE IN COMMON: in each case the COMPUTATION was defensible and the LABEL was not, so no correctness gate could see it - the numbers were all 'right'. Detection has to compare the noun against the aggregation, which is why the gate reads the query shape (head-count vs DISTINCT parent) rather than the value. DISTINCT FROM PMK1, which is about a metric flattering what was DONE; this is about a number being quoted in the wrong UNIT. SWEEP: all three fixed in EN and FIL. GATE: the overdue-noun-scope check covers hive.html's copy and ai-gateway's query shape; teeth proven on both by reverting each.
